Harbour town votes to ban cars from its centre

By Jane Writer

The council of the small harbour town of Eastwick voted on Tuesday to ban private cars from the historic centre starting next spring, ending a debate that has run for almost six years.

Supporters said the move would cut noise and air pollution and make the narrow streets safer for children. Opponents, mostly shop owners, warned that fewer visitors would arrive and that deliveries would become harder to organise.

What changes

  • Private cars are banned between 8am and 8pm.
  • Residents keep access with a permit.
  • Delivery vans may enter before 10am.

The mayor said a review would be held after twelve months and the ban could be adjusted if shop revenue fell by more than ten percent compared with the previous year.

We are not closing the town, we are opening it up to people,

Similar schemes in other coastal towns have been credited with raising footfall, though studies disagree on the effect on retail income, and the council has promised to publish its own data every quarter.
